specPoints.text: understand the effects of deforestation, including leaching, soil erosion, disturbance of evapotranspiration and the carbon cycle, and the balance of atmospheric gases

primer.text: Felling forests damages far more than the trees. This note works through the effects of deforestation: minerals leaching out of bare soil, soil erosion without roots, disturbed evapotranspiration reducing rainfall, and a carbon cycle pushed towards more atmospheric carbon dioxide.

lessons.title: When Forests Fall
lessons.opening: Clearing forest on a large scale does more than remove trees: minerals wash out of unprotected soil, the soil itself erodes, transpiration and the carbon cycle are disturbed, and the balance of atmospheric gases shifts towards warming.
keyPoints: Deforestation means clearing trees across a large area, usually to open land for farming or building.
Leaching increases because no tree roots take up the soil minerals, so rain washes them into water bodies.
Soil erosion increases because roots and organic matter no longer hold the soil together.
Fewer trees mean less transpiration, less cloud formation and less carbon dioxide removed from the air.

low.restatement: No roots means minerals wash out, soil blows away, less vapour rises, and less carbon dioxide is soaked up.
low.analogy: Removing the sponges and the netting from a hillside in a rainstorm.
low.examPointer: The four named effects are leaching, soil erosion, evapotranspiration disturbance and the carbon balance — quote all four.

medium.restatement: Each effect chains from tree loss: uptake stops so minerals leach into water; binding roots and organic matter vanish so soil erodes; transpiration drops so cloud formation and rainfall fall; photosynthesis drops while combustion of felled trees rises, so atmospheric carbon dioxide climbs.
medium.analogy: A warehouse crew fired: stock washes out the door, the shelving collapses, the roof vents close, and the fire in the yard burns the remaining stock.
medium.examPointer: For the carbon effect, state both halves — less removal by photosynthesis and more release by combustion.

options.text: Clearing trees across a large area, usually for farming or building
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: The natural fall of dead leaves
options.explanation: Leaf fall is natural; deforestation clears whole forest stands.
Planting adds trees; deforestation removes them.
Grassland drying is not tree clearing.

check.stem: Why does leaching rise after trees are felled?

options.text: No roots take up the soil minerals, so rain washes them into nearby water
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Rain continues; uptake is what stops.
Minerals are washed away, not multiplied.
Acidity is not the stated mechanism.

check.stem: What holds soil in place inside a healthy forest?

options.text: Tree roots together with organic matter
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Wind actually exposes bare soil once trees fall.
Fungi help, but roots plus organic matter are the named anchors.
Rock lies below the soil; it does not bind the surface.

check.stem: How does felling trees disturb the water cycle?

options.text: Reduced transpiration releases less water vapour, so cloud formation and rainfall fall
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: Trees store all rain in trunks
options.explanation: Trunks do not bank rainfall; transpiration is the pathway.
The effect works through reduced vapour, not instant loss.
No such permanent change is described.

check.stem: Why does deforestation add carbon dioxide to the atmosphere twice over?

options.text: Less photosynthesis removes less carbon dioxide, and burning felled trees releases more
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Trees exhale carbon dioxide when alive
options.explanation: Living trees absorb it during photosynthesis.
The named route is carbon dioxide via photosynthesis loss and combustion.
Fermentation is not the documented mechanism.

check.stem: State the term for soil being washed and blown away after tree removal.
check.modelAnswer: Soil erosion is the term for soil being washed or blown away once roots and organic matter no longer hold it.

check.stem: Name the process by which trees release water vapour into the air.
check.modelAnswer: Transpiration is the process by which trees release water vapour into the atmosphere.

check.stem: Explain why cleared forest land loses fertility quickly.
check.modelAnswer: Cleared land loses fertility because leaching washes away soil minerals and erosion strips the soil itself, leaving little for new growth.

check.stem: A logging company burns its felled timber on site. State two atmospheric effects.
check.modelAnswer: The burning releases carbon dioxide by combustion, and with fewer trees standing, less carbon dioxide is removed by photosynthesis.

glossary.definition: The large-scale clearing of trees, usually to open land for farming or building.
The washing of soil minerals out of the ground by rain into nearby water bodies.
The washing and blowing away of soil no longer held together by roots and organic matter.
The release of water vapour into the atmosphere from the leaves of plants.
